note: Benchmark 2026: institutional values prepared from public, citable datasets for the indicators the SADC workbook leaves empty or carries with values that failed validation. Applied by the engine as approved institutional values (lineage shown), supersedable through the data portal; the workbook itself is unchanged.

HA.NAT.CH-SEA.name: Sea level rise: low-elevation coastal zone (share of area at or below 10 m)
HA.NAT.CH-SEA.basis: Template indicator 'Sea Level Rise' activated with the low-elevation coastal zone share; range resolved from the Tanzanian data as the workbook does

HA.NAT.HW-EXP.name: Heatwave days (runs of 3 or more days above the local 90th percentile), 2015-2024
HA.NAT.HW-EXP.basis: Template indicator 'Heatwave exposure' activated with the warm-spell day count; range resolved from the Tanzanian data

HA.NAT.LI-CAS.name: Lightning stroke density (WWLLN 2010-2021)
HA.NAT.LI-CAS.basis: Template indicator 'Lightning casualties' activated with the stroke density; range resolved from the Tanzanian data

HA.HUM.ACC.name: Road traffic crashes per 100 km2 (police records 2024-2025, shared by population)
HA.HUM.ACC.basis: Template indicator 'Vehicle Accidents' activated with the density of recorded crashes; log-transformed, as the workbook does for its counts; range resolved from the Tanzanian data

HA.HUM.HMAT.name: Hazardous-material sites per 100 km2 (OpenStreetMap, 2022 census, NEMC 2026)
HA.HUM.HMAT.basis: Template indicator 'Hazardous Material' activated with the density of hazardous-material sites; log-transformed, as the workbook does for its counts; range resolved from the Tanzanian data

VU.SE.LV-IPC.name: IPC acute food insecurity area phase
VU.SE.LV-IPC.basis: Template indicator 'Food Security - IPC Classification' activated on the IPC area-phase scale

VU.VG.ECO-FEMHH.name: Female-headed households (2022 census)
VU.VG.ECO-FEMHH.basis: Template indicator activated with the census; range resolved from the Tanzanian data

VU.VG.HC-DISAB.name: People living with disabilities (2022 census)
VU.VG.HC-DISAB.basis: Template indicator activated with the census; range resolved from the Tanzanian data

CC.INS.DRR-ARR.name: DRM arrangements in place (EPRP, RVCA, trained ERT, EOCC, DRR training)
CC.INS.DRR-ARR.basis: Tanzanian indicator in the DRR implementation component: the share of five arrangements, on a fixed 0 to 100 scale (all in place scores 0 lack of coping)

CC.INS.GOV-DMC.name: Disaster management committee functioning (active, stakeholder collaboration, involvement in DRR)
CC.INS.GOV-DMC.basis: Tanzanian indicator in the Governance component: the share of the assessed committee criteria met, on a fixed 0 to 100 scale

VU.SE.LV-FS.basis: The workbook resolved this percentage's range from its own data (0 to 149); a share of population runs from 0 to 100

coastal-erosion.name: Coastal Erosion
coastal-erosion.source: Digital Earth Africa Coastlines v0.4.4 (WFS layer coastlines_v0_4_4_hotspots_zoom_3), Landsat 2000-2023
coastal-erosion.dataset: DE Africa Coastlines v0.4.4, 1 km hotspots: mean annual rate of change over significantly retreating segments
coastal-erosion.method: scripts/benchmark/coastal_exposure.py + build-benchmark.py: 1 km hotspot points (certainty good) joined to the nearest council within 1.5 km; the council value is the point-count-weighted mean of rate_time over segments retreating significantly (rate < 0, p < 0.05); 0 where no segment retreats; inland councils (more than 500 m from the Indian Ocean polygon) 0
coastal-erosion.note: Replaces the workbook's coastal erosion values (0 for every unit, data note DN-05) with the same source correctly joined to the councils.

coastal-lecz.name: Sea Level Rise
coastal-lecz.source: Copernicus DEM GLO-90 (2021 release, AWS public tiles) with the 2022 PHC council boundaries
coastal-lecz.dataset: Low-elevation coastal zone: share of the council's land at or below 10 m within 25 km of the sea
coastal-lecz.method: scripts/benchmark/coastal_exposure.py: GLO-90 tiles mosaicked; cells with elevation 0-10 m inside the council and within 25 km of the Indian Ocean polygon, divided by the council's land cells; inland councils 0
coastal-lecz.note: Activates the template's sea-level-rise indicator with the standard exposure measure (the low-elevation coastal zone of CIESIN/McGranahan et al. 2007).

cyclone-swath.name: Cyclone exposure - max speed
cyclone-swath.source: IBTrACS v04r01, South Indian basin (NOAA NCEI), tracks 1980-2026
cyclone-swath.dataset: Share of the council's area inside the gale-force (34 kt) wind swath of any tropical cyclone since 1980
cyclone-swath.method: scripts/benchmark/cyclone_swaths.py: for every track point with sustained wind of 34 kt or more, a circle of the reported 34-kt wind radius (largest quadrant; 100 km when not reported); the union of the circles of all storms intersected with the council polygon
cyclone-swath.note: Replaces the workbook's cyclone exposure (one non-zero unit, Mtwara 18.1%) with an observed-track exposure for every council; the workbook's reference range (0 to 18.1%) is kept, so every council with at least 18.1% of its area inside a swath scores 10.

heatwave-days.name: Heatwave exposure
heatwave-days.source: ERA5-Land daily maximum 2 m temperature 1991-2024 (ECMWF, through Google Earth Engine ECMWF/ERA5_LAND/DAILY_AGGR)
heatwave-days.dataset: Heatwave days per year: days in runs of three or more days above the calendar-day 90th percentile of 1991-2020, mean of 2015-2024
heatwave-days.method: scripts/benchmark/gee_tmax_daily.py (council-mean daily Tmax) + heatwave_days.py (15-day-window percentile, 3-day runs)
heatwave-days.note: Activates the template's heatwave indicator with the WMO/ETCCDI-style warm-spell definition, which is relative to each place's own climate so that the humid coast and islands register as the rest of the country does.

lightning-density.name: Lightning casualities
lightning-density.source: WWLLN Global Lightning Climatology (WGLC) 2010-2021, 5 arc-minute climatology (Kaplan and Lau 2021, Zenodo record 6007052)
lightning-density.dataset: Mean annual lightning stroke density over the council
lightning-density.method: scripts/benchmark/lightning_zonal.py: annual stroke density summed over the monthly climatology, mean of the 5-arc-minute cells touching the council
lightning-density.note: Activates the template's lightning indicator (listed as casualties, for which no register exists) with the physical hazard density; the Lake Victoria basin and the western and southern highlands show the highest densities.

road-crashes.name: Vehicle Accidents
road-crashes.source: NBS and Tanzania Police Force, Crime and Traffic Incidents Statistics January-December 2024 and 2025, Table 3.4 (recorded road traffic crashes by police region); 2022 PHC council populations; council land areas
road-crashes.dataset: Recorded road traffic crashes per 100 km2 of land a year, mean of 2024 and 2025
road-crashes.resolution: council (each police region's crashes shared among its councils by population; the Dar es Salaam and Zanzibar police regions are city-level)
road-crashes.method: scripts/benchmark/road_crashes.py: each police region's recorded crashes (mean of 2024 and 2025) shared among its councils in proportion to their 2022 census population, divided by the council's land area (scripts/benchmark/land_area.py)
road-crashes.note: Activates the template's vehicle-accidents indicator with where crashes happen: the density of crashes is highest in the big cities (Zanzibar Town, the Dar es Salaam municipalities, Moshi, Mbeya, Mwanza, Arusha), where most road-traffic injuries occur (65.7% of 7,092 injured patients in Sawe et al. 2021, Emergency Medicine International, doi:10.1155/2021/4272781). Police records count serious crashes; until 2019 they also counted injury and damage-only crashes, of which Dar es Salaam recorded more than half (NBS 2018, 2019).

hazmat-sites.name: Hazardous Material
hazmat-sites.source: OpenStreetMap (Overpass API, 10 October 2026, ODbL); NBS 2022 Population and Housing Census mapping (small-scale industries, hospitals); NEMC environmental certificates (EIA and audit) issued July-September 2026
hazmat-sites.dataset: Sites that produce, store, process or dispose of hazardous materials per 100 km2 of land: fuel and gas installations, mines and mineral processing, factories and industrial areas, waste and thermal power sites, hospitals
hazmat-sites.method: scripts/benchmark/osm_hazmat.py (OpenStreetMap installations), nemc_certificates.py (the NEMC monthly certificate lists read, placed in their council from the ward and classified) and hazmat_sites.py: mapped points closer than 100 m are one site; certificates added by council; sites divided by the council's land area
hazmat-sites.note: Activates the template's hazardous-material indicator. The cities and their industrial corridors lead (Dar es Salaam, Zanzibar Town, Moshi, Mwanza and Ilemela, Arusha, Tanga, Mbeya, Morogoro, Kibaha and Mkuranga), followed by the gold-mining councils, where the NEMC lists certify carbon-in-pulp plants and tailings facilities. NEMC's Lake Victoria roadmap for Mwanza City (2023) counts 51 industries there and names the Nyashishi river as the carrier of industrial effluent into the lake. A site counts once whatever its size.

ipc-phase2plus.name: Food Security - Insufficient food
ipc-phase2plus.source: IPC Tanzania Acute Food Insecurity Analysis, April 2026 (MUCHALI with the IPC Global Support Unit), population table for February-May 2026
ipc-phase2plus.dataset: Share of the analysed population in IPC Phase 2 or worse, by district
ipc-phase2plus.method: build-benchmark.py from ipc_2026_districts.csv: 100 minus the Phase 1 share; districts matched to councils by the registry's district
ipc-phase2plus.note: Replaces the workbook's food-security values (0 in 127 councils, 149% in one, data note DN-06) for the 30 analysed districts; the reference range is re-resolved to 0-100%.

ipc-area-phase.name: Food Security - IPC Classification
ipc-area-phase.source: IPC Tanzania Acute Food Insecurity Analysis, April 2026 (area classification); districts outside the analysis were not flagged by the national MUCHALI screening of production shortfalls and are classified Minimal (Phase 1)
ipc-area-phase.dataset: IPC area phase (1 Minimal to 5 Famine), February-May 2026
ipc-area-phase.method: build-benchmark.py: the report's area phase for the 30 analysed districts (Crisis where 20% or more of the population is in Phase 3 or worse); Phase 1 elsewhere
ipc-area-phase.note: Activates the template's IPC classification indicator on the IPC's own 1-5 scale.

census-electricity.name: Access to electricity
census-electricity.source: NBS, 2022 Population and Housing Census, Regional Basic Demographic and Socio-Economic Profile reports (31 regions, 2024-2026)
census-electricity.dataset: Households whose main source of lighting is electricity (grid, solar or generator), Table 12.10 of each regional profile
census-electricity.method: scripts/benchmark/census_profiles.py: grid (TANESCO) + solar + generator shares of households by council; where a profile gives only the grid share by council (Pwani, Ruvuma) that share is used
census-electricity.note: Replaces the workbook's regional Global Data Lab values (Dodoma 100%, data note DN-08) with the census by council.

census-phone.name: Cellphone ownership
census-phone.source: NBS, 2022 Population and Housing Census, Regional Basic Demographic and Socio-Economic Profile reports (31 regions, 2024-2026)
census-phone.dataset: Persons aged 15 and above owning a mobile phone, Table 13.2 of each regional profile
census-phone.method: scripts/benchmark/census_profiles.py: 'any mobile phone, both sexes' by council
census-phone.note: Replaces the workbook's regional values with the census by council (persons rather than households).

census-literacy.name: Adult literacy rate
census-literacy.source: NBS, 2022 Population and Housing Census, Regional Basic Demographic and Socio-Economic Profile reports (31 regions, 2024-2026)
census-literacy.dataset: Literacy rate of persons aged 15 and above, 2022, Table 8.5 (8.3 for Dar es Salaam) of each regional profile
census-literacy.method: scripts/benchmark/census_profiles.py: 2022 census, both sexes, by council
census-literacy.note: Replaces the workbook's national literacy value with the census by council.

census-female-headed.name: Female headed households
census-female-headed.source: NBS, 2022 Population and Housing Census, Regional Basic Demographic and Socio-Economic Profile reports (31 regions, 2024-2026)
census-female-headed.dataset: Female-headed households, 2022, Table 4.4 of each regional profile
census-female-headed.method: scripts/benchmark/census_profiles.py: 2022 share of households headed by a woman, by council
census-female-headed.note: Activates the template's female-headed-households indicator with the census.

census-disability.name: People living with disabilities
census-disability.source: NBS, 2022 Population and Housing Census, Regional Basic Demographic and Socio-Economic Profile reports (31 regions, 2024-2026)
census-disability.dataset: Disability prevalence (persons aged 7 and above), Table 10.2 of each regional profile
census-disability.method: scripts/benchmark/census_profiles.py: prevalence, both sexes, by council
census-disability.note: Activates the template's disability indicator with the census.

landslide-ukerewe.name: Landslide exposure
landslide-ukerewe.source: World Bank/GFDRR Global Landslide Hazard Map (Arup 2021), threshold ranks raster LS_TH_COG.tif
landslide-ukerewe.dataset: Share of the council's area in rank 3 or 4 (medium to high landslide hazard)
landslide-ukerewe.method: build-benchmark.py from landslide_wb_ranks.csv: the island has no valid hazard cell in the global map (every cell is water/no-data, which the workbook counted as fully exposed); the share of medium-to-high cells is 0
landslide-ukerewe.note: Replaces the workbook's Ukerewe value (1.0, the national maximum, data note DN-04); the global map's own ranks reproduce the workbook for the other councils (r = 0.77 with the share of rank 3-4 cells).

drr-arrangements.source: PMO-DMD lists of district emergency preparedness and response plans and regional emergency operation centres and response teams (shared June 2026; communication of 10 October 2026), with the published launches and trainings of 2023-2026 (Kinondoni 2023; Mwanza, Mbeya, Arusha, Dodoma 2026) and TMA's bimodal rainfall areas for the trained teams
drr-arrangements.dataset: DRM arrangements in place: share of five (EPRP, RVCA, trained ERT, EOCC, DRR training of the committee)
drr-arrangements.resolution: council (plans and assessments by district; teams, centres and training by region)
drr-arrangements.method: build-benchmark.py from drr_status.csv: a council has its district's plan and assessment, its region's team, centre and training; an arrangement not listed is not in place (the registers are PMO-DMD's own); the share of the five, as src/engine/risk/institutional.ts scores an approved committee record
drr-arrangements.note: Adds a Tanzanian indicator to the workbook's DRR implementation group beside its two national ones (Sendai score, anticipatory-action coverage), so that a council's own preparedness lowers its lack of coping capacity and, through the council means, its region's and the country's (decision of 10 October 2026). The national value is high while the registers are incomplete and falls as PMO-DMD records more districts.

committee-functioning.source: PMO-DMD assessment communicated 10 October 2026 (stakeholder collaboration in the big cities; involvement in DRR issues in Arusha, Mwanza and Pwani) and the published committee trainings of 2023-2026; to be confirmed and completed by the committees through the Data portal
committee-functioning.dataset: Disaster management committee functioning: share of the assessed criteria met (committee active, stakeholder collaboration, involvement in DRR)
committee-functioning.resolution: council (criteria assessed by region or council)
committee-functioning.method: build-benchmark.py from drr_status.csv: a criterion recorded 1 or 0 is assessed; the share of the assessed criteria met; a council with no assessed criterion has no value (the group keeps the workbook's two indicators), as src/engine/risk/institutional.ts scores an approved committee record
committee-functioning.note: Adds a Tanzanian indicator to the workbook's Governance group beside its national government-effectiveness score and regional corruption index. The legal framework (the Disaster Management Act 2022 and the policy) is the same everywhere and is not scored; the differences PMO-DMD sees are in collaboration and involvement.

idmc-idp.name: Internal Displaced People
idmc-idp.source: IDMC Global Internal Displacement Database (disaster IDP stock, end of 2024) and IDMC Internal Displacement Updates for Tanzania 2023-2025 (event locations and figures), external API
idmc-idp.dataset: Disaster IDPs at the end of 2024 allocated to regions by the location of the 2023-2025 displacement events
idmc-idp.method: build-benchmark.py: 23 displacement updates with a region or district in their location; an update naming several regions is split equally; the national stock of 75,117 is allocated in proportion to each region's share of the 2023-2025 displacements; regions without a recorded displacement 0
idmc-idp.note: Replaces the workbook's displacement values (the national stock of 30,080 written on Kaskazini Unguja alone, Manyara 0 after the Hanang landslide; data note DN-07) with a documented regional allocation of IDMC's own figures.
